title: The Uncapped Advantage: Finding Low-Cost Impact for Lucknow Super Giants
dek: Where can Lucknow Super Giants find impact for a fraction of the purse? Players bought for ₹1 Cr or less since 2018 show how often the bargain bin delivers.
excerpt: Lucknow Super Giants have carried a stream of low-cost players since 2018. Only some got a real chance, and fewer still beat the league average, but the ones who did are the cheapest contribution in the squad.

sections.heading: The Bargain Bin
body: Every squad carries players bought near their base price. Most are cover; a few become regulars and produce far more than their price suggests. Finding them is the cheapest edge in the auction.

sections.heading: Finding the Next One
body: Low-cost success usually follows a pattern: a domestic player with a strong record in one role, given a defined job. The risk is in giving cheap players undefined roles or no opportunities at all.
For LSG, each low-cost signing should come with a planned role and a minimum number of chances.

sections.heading: Opportunity Bias
body: Low-cost players who play are those whom coaches already trusted, so their record overstates what an untested cheap signing would deliver.

sections.heading: CricField Verdict: Fewer Bargains, Clearer Roles
body: Lucknow Super Giants should carry fewer low-cost players but give each a defined role. The data shows the bargain bin delivers when players get chances.
Domestic performance in the specific role is the scouting signal to weight most.

methodology: Contribution is tempo runs above average (tRAA): batting runs above what an average batter would score from the same balls in the same season and phase, plus bowling runs saved against the average bowler in the same season and phase. Wickets and dismissals are not valued in this version. Prices come from CricField squad lists (₹ crore = 100 lakh). Generated by scripts/editorial/engine. Low cost = recorded price of ₹1 Cr or less.
